title: A torch beam tilted under water
hook: From under water, tilt a torch further and further. Does its light always get out?

knows: light bends when it crosses from water into air
doesNotKnow: that some light always reflects at a surface, and that past a certain tilt all of it does

misconception: Some light always gets through a boundary between water and air.
objective: The learner can explain that light leaving water bends away from straight up, more than it is tilted, and that beyond about 48.6 degrees there is no exit direction left, so all of it reflects back down.

claims.text: Light crossing from water into air bends away from straight up, following Snell's law: 1.333 × sin(angle in water) = 1.00 × sin(angle in air).
claims.source: OpenStax College Physics 2e, section 25.3 The Law of Refraction (Snell's law; n water = 1.333, n air = 1.000293, taken as 1.00).

claims.text: The critical angle for water to air is 48.6° from straight up; there the exit direction lies flat along the surface (90°) and no light gets out; beyond it there is no exit direction and all of it reflects back down (total internal reflection).
claims.source: sin(theta_c) = 1.00 / 1.333 = 0.750, theta_c = 48.61 degrees (node). OpenStax College Physics 2e, section 25.4 Total Internal Reflection gives 48.6 degrees for water. · Fact-check pass 21 2026-10-14: asin(1/1.333) = 48.607°, shown as 48.6°. At that stop snell() returns 90 and fresnel() returns 1; beyond it snell() returns null. OpenStax 2e 25.4 not reachable (DNS blocked); the number rests on Snell's law.

claims.text: At 45° in water the beam leaves at 70.5° from straight up; at 47°, at 77.1°; at 48°, at 82.1°; at 30°, at 41.8°.
Below the critical angle some light still reflects: about 2% straight up, 14% at 45°, 26% at 47°, 43% at 48°, rising to 100% at 48.6°; the stage labels the reflected ray with this share.
claims.source: Fresnel equations, unpolarised average of rs and rp (Hecht, Optics, §4.6). Node over Demo.tsx v3 fresnel(): 0° 0.020, 45° 0.139, 47° 0.261, 48° 0.433, 48.6° 1. · Fact-check pass 21 2026-10-14: Own Fresnel rs, rp (formulae re-derived: rs = ((n1 cos i - n2 cos t)/(n1 cos i + n2 cos t))², rp = ((n2 cos i - n1 cos t)/(n2 cos i + n1 cos t))², n1 = 1.333, n2 = 1): 0° 0.0204, 45° 0.1395, 47° 0.2614, 48° 0.4331, critical 1. Hecht not opened.

claims.text: Idealisations: a still, flat surface and light of one colour; absorption in the water is ignored.
claims.source: Stated on stage ('Still, flat surface') and in the reveal. Refractive index varies slightly with colour (dispersion), shifting the critical angle by a fraction of a degree.

recall.question: A diver looks up at the water's surface at a slant far from straight up. Instead of the sky she sees...
options: A reflection of the pool below, as in a mirror
recall.why: Past the critical angle (about 49 degrees from straight up) light cannot leave the water, so the surface reflects all of it back down like a perfect mirror.
